high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. When I choose a goal, I tend to move straight toward it and turn the plan into concrete action. Having a possibility in mind is usually a starting point for doing something about it. I care about making progress toward what I want to achieve, even when the goal is private or the work is unpaid.

I put substantial time and effort into my work and often throw myself into a task wholeheartedly. I can find it hard to be satisfied with a merely adequate contribution. When the expected amount would be enough to get by, I commonly add something extra because I want the result to go further.

I set high standards for myself and for people working with me. I demand quality, notice shortcomings and may press for another revision when others would settle. This can make me exacting or difficult to satisfy. I am strongly motivated to succeed, and achievement matters to me; recognition or advancement may be welcome without being the only reason I strive.

These tendencies allow ordinary exceptions, limitations and failures. They do not guarantee talent, good judgment, fair treatment or flawless persistence. Describe my own motives and behavior in the requested format, rather than turning them into productivity advice, an ideal employee story or a moral ranking.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. When I consider a goal, I often leave it at the level of a possibility rather than direct my behavior toward it. A plan may stay on paper without becoming concrete action. I do not usually organize my choices around making substantial progress toward an achievement, even when the goal is private and resources are available.

I put relatively little time and effort into my work and often engage with a task halfheartedly. I am generally satisfied with a contribution that gets by. When the expected amount is sufficient, I rarely add something extra just to push the result further, even if I could do more.

I keep my standards for myself and people working with me undemanding. An ordinary, imperfect result can be enough; I seldom press for another revision in pursuit of higher quality. I am not strongly motivated to succeed, and achievement is not a major organizing concern. Recognition or advancement may be available without giving me much reason to strive.

These tendencies allow ordinary exceptions, interests and responsibilities. They do not guarantee dishonesty, incapacity, broken promises or an inability to finish a simple chore. Describe my own motives and behavior in the requested format, rather than turning them into a diagnosis, an excuse imposed by poverty or a moral ranking.
